title.narrative: Supporting Gas Project Negotiations and Enhancing Institutional Capacities

description.narrative: Support the government's capacity to drive negotiations towards final investments decisions and lay the foundations for the gas sector's contributions to the economy through enhanced legal and regulatory framework and capacity building.

The development objective of the Supporting Gas Project Negotiations and Enhancing Institutional Capacities Project for Senegal is to support the government's capacity to drive negotiations towards final investments decisions and lay the foundations for the gas sector's contributions to the economy through enhanced legal and regulatory framework and capacity building.The project consists of five components. The first component, support for hydrocarbon project negotiations the objective of this component is to help the Government of Senegal (GoSN) engage in a timely and constructive manner with the Government of Mauritania and Production Sharing Contract (PSC) holders to ensure the sustainable development of its oil and gas resources. The second component, enhancement of the strategic and policy framework is to support the GoSN develop an oil and gas sector policy and strategy. The third component, institutional diagnostic and capacity building is to identify the needs for capacity building, develop tailored training programs, and support the Government's effort to mobilize instrumental ad hoc expertise. The fourth component, stakeholders engagement campaign is to mobilize international third party expertise needed for the GoSN to develop a communications strategy and information campaign to engage effectively and sustain ably with all key stakeholders on issues relating to oil and gas development projects in SNE and Grand Tortue. This component, which will create and maximize synergies with the Senegal Extractive Industry Transparency Initiative (EITI) activity on communications campaign.

condition.narrative: (Schedule 2.I.A.1 - amended) The Recipient shall maintain, until completion of the Project, a Project Steering Committee, withterms of reference, mandate, resources and composition satisfactory to the Association. The Project Steering Committee shall be:(a) chaired by the Minister of Petroleum and-Energy, (b) composed of representatives of the Recipient's Ministry of Finance andBudget, Ministry of Economy, Plan and Co-operation, Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development, Ministry of Fisheries andMaritime Economy and Ministry of Petroleum and Energy, and representatives of PETROSEN and COS-Petrogaz, and ( c) responsible forinter alia (i) providing strategic orientation for the Project and supervising its implementation; (ii) reviewing and adopting theAnnual Work Plan in accordance with Section I.D. of this Schedule; and (iii) formulating recommendations and proposals tofacilitate Project implementation

(Schedule 2.I.B.1) The Recipient shall: (i) through PETROSEN, carry out the Project in accordance with PETROSEN Project Manual;(ii) through GES-PETROGAZ, shall adopt, not later than six (6) months after the Effective Date, a revised Project Manualsatisfactory to the Association; and (iii) not amend, abrogate, waive or permit to be amended, abrogated or waived, theaforementioned Project Manual, or any provision thereof, without the prior written consent of the Association.

(Schedule 2.I.E.1) The Recipient shall ensure that a Master Plan for Oil and Gas Development is prepared in accordance with termsof reference approved by the Association. If the Master Plan for Oil and Gas Development is finalized during Projectimplementation, the Recipient shall prepare a Strategic Environmental and Social Assessment of the oil and gas sector acceptable tothe Association.

(Schedule 2.II.B.4) The Recipient shall by not later than six (6) months after the Effective Date: (i) select one external auditorand one internal auditor, both with qualifications satisfactory to the Association; and (ii) recruit an accountant pursuant totermsof reference and with qualifications and experience satisfactory to the Association.

title.narrative: High level training completed for institutional capacity building

comment.narrative: Participants to training sessions so far have included Ministry of Petroleum and Energy and Ministry of Finance staff. The former Minister of Energy participated to one session.

title.narrative: Staff trained in oil and gas law and oil contracts management

comment.narrative: Staff from the legal and contract management departments of PETROSEN, MPE, and MFB

title.narrative: Staff trained in petroleum taxation and accounting

comment.narrative: Accountant and tax specialists from PETROSEN, MPE, and MFB and SP-COS-PETROGAZ

title.narrative: Intergovernmental cooperation agreement developed and signed

comment.narrative: Intergovernmental cooperation agreement for joint development of Grand Tortue reservoir with Mauritania developed by the Government using technical expertise provided by international experts, and the final agreement is approved by the Government.

title.narrative: Delineation and estimation of transnational gas finalized

comment.narrative: Unitized delineation and estimation of the transnational gas resource area regarding the Grand Tortue reservoir produced by international experts recruited by the Government.

title.narrative: Assessment on the current existing communications options/mechanisms and institutional capacity regarding communications conducted

comment.narrative: Assessment on the current existing communications options/mechanisms and institutional capacity regarding communications in key ministries conducted by experts recruited by the Government.

title.narrative: Communications strategy and roadmap for government agencies developed and implemented

comment.narrative: A firm was hired to complete the communication strategy and has presented an inception report for validation.

title.narrative: Unitization agreement for the Grand Tortue reservoir developed

comment.narrative: A unitization agreement for the joint development of the GTA reservoir with Mauritania is developed by the government using technical expertise provided by international experts.

title.narrative: Development concept for phase 1 of Grand Tortue Ahmeyim and Sangomar validated

comment.narrative: Development concepts completed and validated. Both projects are producing hydrocarbons since late 2024 (Sangomar) and early 2025 (GTA).

title.narrative: Institutional diagnostic conducted and results publicly disseminated

comment.narrative: Institutional diagnostic of key ministries and PETROSEN conducted by international experts recruited by the Government, with findings of the diagnostic being available to the general public.

title.narrative: A regulatory framework for the integration of off-shore projects into the maritime economy is developed

comment.narrative: The regulatory framework to ensure the safety of artisanal fishery is in place, and the manual for inspection of platforms and floating installations was completed and adopted. The law on commercial shipping is readily prepared and currently with the government for review and approval before being submitted to parliament.

title.narrative: Training completed for institutional capacity building

comment.narrative: 485 (against the target of 500) project beneficiaries who received training. This indicator refers to trainings provided within the framework of consulting contracts, covering the following areas: - Offshore engineering aspects (GTA, SANGOMAR) - Major stages of an oil and gas development project - Liquefaction of natural gas - Different types of seabed-to-surface connections - Fundamentals of flow assurance - Fundamentals of availability studies - Risk prevention in the O&G industry - Implementation and design of an onshore site - Monitoring environmental standards - Measurement and characteristics of liquids and gases - Legal metrology: regulations applicable to liquids and gases - LNG value chain economics - Economic models for O&G valorization projects - ARCGIS and QGIS - Modeling oil and gas fiscal revenues - Economic, contractual, and fiscal framework of O&G operations - Oil and gas value chain economics - Establishing a petroleum register

title.narrative: Lifting agreement for Sangomar Phase 1 in place

comment.narrative: Lifting agreements for Sangomar Phase 1 is developed by international experts recruited by the Government

title.narrative: Key staff recruited to fill the technical capacity gap

comment.narrative: Staff for the role of Oil and gas development advisor, upstream expert, upstream engineer, petroleum architecture engineer, oil and gas operations monitoring expert, petroleum cost engineer, expert in reservoir engineering.

title.narrative: Strategic Environnemental and Social Assessment completed

comment.narrative: The SESA was completed, reviewed by the ESF functions and confirmed by RSA.

title.narrative: A transparent system for the award of oil and gas exploration and production rights is established

comment.narrative: The oil and gas cadaster is developed and functional

title.narrative: Framework for the monitoring and evaluation of environmental and social impacts of oil and gas operations is in place

comment.narrative: The majority of the components under this activity have been completed notably: (i) environmental atlas; (ii) docking study; (iii) geographic information system. Item (iv) (Prevention plan for water and air pollution) is complete but has not yet been formally issued through a decree or an arret.

title.narrative: Master plan for the oil and gas sector is developed

comment.narrative: The master plan for the development of the oil and gas sector is prepared by the Government
